notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Sources: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001543151-26-000015, filed February 13, 2026) and the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001308179-26-000125, filed March 23, 2026), read on EDGAR. Uber's 10-K tables list years in ascending order (2023, 2024, 2025), so the 2025 value is the last number in each quote. LEADER: Khosrowshahi is a hired CEO. He beneficially owns 2,380,203 shares as of March 2, 2026 (982,544 held, 496,958 RSUs vesting within 60 days, 900,701 exercisable options), marked * (less than 1%), so pctEconomic is null. HOLDERS: the proxy gives only the filing dates of the 13G reports (Vanguard Schedule 13G/A October 31, 2025; BlackRock January 26, 2024, stale; Capital Research February 13, 2025), not their as-of dates, so asOf is null; percentages use the March 2, 2026 share count. STOCK COMP: 1,826 is the cash-flow add-back and the XBRL ShareBasedCompensation fact. BUYBACKS rose to 6,523 in 2025 from 1,252 in 2024. GEOGRAPHY: the country table (United States, United Kingdom, all other countries) is used, as in the prior edition; the same note now also gives a regional table (US&CAN 26,469, LatAm 3,327, EMEA 16,364, APAC 5,857 million). U.K. revenue is presented largely on a gross basis since Uber became the merchant of transportation there in 2022 (payments to drivers go into cost of revenue).

ecosystem.notes: Gross Bookings include Freight revenue, which Uber books gross, as well as taxes, tolls and fees. They exclude tips. Revenue includes Freight revenue. The 10-K does not state total driver or courier earnings, so payouts is null. 'Platform Participant direct transaction costs' (costs paid to Platform Earners that Uber records in cost of revenue, plus end-user incentives) are a partial, mixed amount, not total earnings, and are not used.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Uber presents revenue on a gross basis in markets where it is responsible for the Mobility, Delivery or Freight service, with payments to drivers and carriers in cost of revenue, so revenue ÷ Gross Bookings overstates what Uber keeps.

footprint.notes: No U.S. state breakdown exists on uber.com. Checked 2026-11-24: Uber's sitemap index and the us_en, global_en, ca_en, nz_en, bd_en, gb_en, lk_en and zh-tw sitemaps for impact, economic and economy newsroom pages. The commissioned country reports are unchanged because no newer edition was found (checked 2026-11-24): Canada's newest is the 2024 report (older ones are 2022 and 2023, plus British Columbia 2023), New Zealand's is 2024, Bangladesh's is 2024 (older: 2021), Sri Lanka's is the 2024 report cited in the Dec 2025 post (older: 2021), Taiwan's is the year ending September 2024 (older: 2023), and the UK's newest is the Sep 2023 post about 2022. The U.S. Uber Eats figures come from the 2025 U.S. Merchant Impact Report (2024 data); no 2026 edition was found. State posts on the U.S. newsroom date from 2015-2018 or are advocacy pieces, and the U.S. 'Uber in the economy' page cites an undated EDR Group study, not used. Country rows are Public First estimates commissioned by Uber, each in its own currency, so they are separate metrics and not comparable. CA and NZ amounts appear only as '$' on the local pages and are read as local dollars. India's 'INR 36,000 crores' is a forecast for Auto and Moto only and was skipped. Employees: the FY2025 10-K gives ~34,000 global employees at Dec 31, 2025, of whom ~20,300 were outside the U.S.; that is stored as a region and no U.S. figure was derived.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001543151-26-000015). Marketplace: salesEnabled = Gross Bookings − revenue. In gross (principal) markets and Freight the fare is in both Gross Bookings and revenue and nets to zero, and driver pay is counted once, through paidOut; in agent markets driver earnings sit outside revenue and are counted once, through salesEnabled. Gross Bookings include taxes, tolls and fees and are before consumer discounts (overstates). Interest and income taxes paid are inside operating cash flow (US GAAP); the 10-K still prints both in the supplemental cash-flow disclosures, and the income-tax note gives the same 345 total by jurisdiction (US federal 12, US state and local 81, foreign 252).

pay.notes: Employees: approximate year-end count from the FY2025 10-K; drivers and couriers are independent platform users, not employees. Payroll: the FY2025 10-K discloses no total staff cost, so the proxy's CEO pay ratio median for fiscal 2025 is used (CEO pay ratio 360 to 1). The median was identified from 33,354 employees at November 1, 2025, about 99% full-time, excluding about 450 employees who joined through the DanTaxi, Trendyol Go and Segments.ai acquisitions; compensation was converted to U.S. dollars at the exchange rate on that date.
